items.title: Health unit in northwestern Ontario confirms measles case, capping a year of alarming rise in Canadian cases
items.description: The Northwestern Health Unit has confirmed a case of measles in the Kenora area of northwestern Ontario, in a year that saw an alarming rise in cases in Canada and the country lose its measles elimination status.

items.title: Duty free shops say they're still losing sales as Canada-U.S. cross-border travel plummets
items.description: Owners of duty free shops in Windsor and Sarnia say they continue to suffer the fall-out from the U.S. trade war, seeing drops in business in the 30 per cent range year over year.

items.title: Canada, other nations call on Israel to ensure aid groups can work in Gaza
items.description: Canada and other nations are calling on Israel to boost the flow of humanitarian aid into Gaza as the country reportedly moves to suspend more than two dozen organizations.

items.title: Father says son killed as Sask. RCMP search for armed pair on Big Island Lake Cree Nation
items.description: At least one man is dead and police are searching for two armed men on Big Island Lake Cree Nation, CBC News has learned. Saskatchewan RCMP are telling people living on the First Nation near the Alberta border to find a safe location immediately and lock their doors.

items.title: Alberta’s Health-Care Privatization Push Is Heading to Disaster
items.description: The UCP government has chosen a discredited ideology over real solutions.

items.title: Couple from Gatineau, Que., found dead while vacationing in Dominican Republic
items.description: The son of Alain Noël and Christine Sauvé found their bodies inside the couple's vacation home on Boxing Day, the family told Radio-Canada.

items.title: 'Frustration at its pinnacle:' Ontario newcomers anxious over immigration overhaul
items.description: Concerned about recent changes to immigration in Ontario, Muhammad Haseeb Ahmad is anxiously awaiting word on whether he can become a Canadian permanent resident.

items.title: Pimicikamak Cree Nation declares state of emergency after power outage in northern Manitoba
items.description: Residents of a northern Manitoba First Nation are being told that their power will not be restored until late in the day on New Year’s Eve. Pimicikamak Cree Nation declared a state of emergency on Monday following a widespread power outage in the Cross Lake area around 11:30 p.m. Sunday.

items.title: Green Party settles with commission over exclusion from federal leaders' debate
items.description: The federal Leaders' Debates Commission says it has settled with the Green Party after the party vowed to challenge its removal from the spring election debates.

items.title: What's coming up next in Canadian politics? Here are five key stories to watch in 2026
items.description: 2026 is shaping up to be an action-packed year in Canadian politics. Federal opposition parties will make key decisions on their futures as the Liberal government, just one seat shy of a majority government, strategizes what to do next while juggling U.S. trade talks. Here are five key stories to keep an eye on next year.

items.title: Thousands still without power after winter storm in Ontario, utility says
items.description: Hydro One says challenging road conditions are slowing down crews in some areas, and its outage map shows some 15,000 customers remain without power as of this morning.

items.title: Human remains found in community east of North Bay, Ont., police say
items.description: OPP say they were called Sunday morning to an area in Head, Clara and Maria Township after the remains were discovered.

items.title: Hiring managers surveyed remain ‘cautious' about the 2026 job market
items.description: A quarter of hiring managers surveyed say they are 'cautious' about their ability to hire more workers in 2026, according to newly released data.
